info.title: API.SH: Messari
info.description: The Messari API from API.SH: public Messari data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
One crypto asset in full: market data (price, changes, market cap, FDV, volume, supply, dominance, all-time high and cycle low with dates, 30-day and 1-year volatility, 1-year Sharpe ratio), derivatives (open interest, funding rate, futures volume), number of exchanges and markets, mindshare rank and sentiment, genesis date, tags, links and team members (name, title, links); the project profile (overview, background, sector, sub-sectors, FAQs, links, logo); and the token unlock summary (percent unlocked, next cliff unlock date, amount and share of circulating supply, daily emissions, unlocked and remaining value, allocation by recipient, inflation details).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/messari-asset

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: Asset slug (`ethereum`, `binance-coin`), project slug (`bnb-chain`), ticker symbol (`ETH`; the highest-ranked asset with that symbol) or name.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Crypto assets ranked by market cap with Messari's market data: name, symbol, slug, rank, live price, price change over 1 hour, 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days and 1 year, market cap, fully diluted market cap, 24-hour volume, circulating, total and max supply, market cap dominance, all-time high and percent below it, sector and sub-sector; plus any extra field from the asset field list. Filter by sector, sub-sector, symbol and market cap range; sort by any returned field. Returns the total. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; it is null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/messari-assets

parameters.name: sector
parameters.description: Sector name as in /messari/v1/sectors, e.g. `DeFi`, `Networks`, `AI`, `Stablecoins`.

parameters.name: sub_sector
parameters.description: Sub-sector name, e.g. `Layer-1`, `Lending`, `DEX`.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Ticker symbol, e.g. `DOGE` (several assets can share one).

parameters.name: min_market_cap
parameters.description: Minimum market cap in USD.

parameters.name: max_market_cap
parameters.description: Maximum market cap in USD.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort field (default `market_cap`); any returned column label also works.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort order (default `desc`; `asc` for rank and days to the next unlock).

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: Extra fields, comma separated, by id or label from /messari/v1/fields?dataset=asset (e.g. `GitHub Stars,Twitter Followers,Volatility (30D)`); returned under their label.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; it is null on the last page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page (default 50, max 200).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

Every field Messari's screener has for assets, projects, exchanges, sectors or markets: id, label (as returned), name, category (market data, token unlocks, developer activity, derivatives, stablecoins, mindshare and more), type, format and description. Use the ids in `columns=` and `sort=` of the list routes.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/messari-fields

get.description:
Price candles for a crypto asset: time, open, high, low, close and volume in USD at 5-minute, 15-minute, hourly, daily or weekly intervals, for the last N days or between two dates. Up to 2 days of 5-minute, 7 days of 15-minute, 90 days of hourly, 3 years of daily and 10 years of weekly candles per call.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/messari-price-history

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: Asset slug (`ethereum`, `binance-coin`), project slug (`bnb-chain`), ticker symbol (`ETH`; the highest-ranked asset with that symbol) or name.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Candle size (default `1d`).

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: The last N days (default 365 for daily, 1825 for weekly, the maximum otherwise).

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start date `YYYY-MM-DD` instead of days.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End date `YYYY-MM-DD` (default today).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Crypto assets with upcoming token unlocks, soonest first: name, symbol, rank, price, market cap, percent unlocked, next cliff unlock (date and the allocations it releases), days to it, its value in USD and as a share of circulating supply, daily emissions, unlocked and remaining value, genesis and projected end date. Pass `upcoming=false` for every asset with an unlock schedule. Returns the total. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; it is null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/messari-token-unlocks

parameters.name: upcoming
parameters.description: `true` (default): only assets with a next cliff unlock; `false`: every asset with an unlock schedule.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort field (default `days_to_next_cliff`, soonest first).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort order (default `desc`; `asc` for rank and days to the next unlock).

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: Extra fields, comma separated, by id or label from /messari/v1/fields?dataset=asset (e.g. `GitHub Stars,Twitter Followers,Volatility (30D)`); returned under their label.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; it is null on the last page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page (default 50, max 200).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
